hero.title: Practice the Basics
intro.0: Foundations gave you values, variables and objects. Here you put them to work: compute with numbers, join text, and - the step toward Control Flow - ask yes/no questions with comparisons that give back a bool. Write and run each one.
task.1.title: Do math with variables
task.1.context:
You can compute with values using the arithmetic operators:

- `+` - add
- `-` - subtract
- `*` - multiply
- `/` - divide
- `%` - remainder

Combine variables and you get a new value back.

`%` is the one that trips people up: it is not a percentage. `14 % 4` is 2 - 4 fits into 14 three whole times and 2 is left over. And C# has no power operator, so `2 ** 10` will not compile; you call `Math.Pow(2, 10)` instead.
task.1.goal.1: Print `apples * baskets`. The output should be 12.
task.1.goal.2: Then make `int treats = 14` and print `treats % baskets` - what is left over. The output should be 2.
task.2.title: Join text
task.2.context: `+` also joins strings end to end - this is called concatenation. `"Hi, " + name` builds one string from two pieces. You can join a number onto a string too; it becomes text.
task.2.goal.1: Print `"Good dog, " + name`. The output should be Good dog, Rex.
task.3.title: Ask a yes/no question
task.3.context:
A **comparison** asks a yes/no question and gives back a `bool`:

- `==` - equal
- `!=` - not equal
- `>` `<` `>=` `<=` - greater / less than (or equal to)

So `age >= 18` is `true` when age is 18 or more. Watch the difference: `==` compares, a single `=` stores.
task.3.goal.1: Make `bool isAdult = age >= 18`, then print `isAdult`. The output should be True.
task.4.title: An object that answers about itself
task.4.context: Put state and a comparison together. A `Thermostat` knows its `Temp` (state) and can answer `IsHot()` (behaviour) by comparing that state. The method returns the `bool` a comparison produces - an object reporting something about itself.
task.4.goal.1: Make `IsHot()` return whether `Temp` is greater than `25`.
task.4.goal.2: `Main` builds one and prints `IsHot()`. The output should be True.
task.5.title: Practice the Basics recap
task.5.summaryIntro: You put the Foundations pieces to work and reached the doorway to Control Flow.
task.5.summaryItems.0.title: Arithmetic -
task.5.summaryItems.0.text: `+ - * / %` compute a new value from existing ones. `%` is the remainder, not a percentage.
task.5.summaryItems.1.title: Concatenation -
task.5.summaryItems.1.text: `+` joins strings (and numbers) into one string.
task.5.summaryItems.2.title: Comparison -
task.5.summaryItems.2.text: `==` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` ask a yes/no question and return a `bool`.
task.5.summaryItems.3.title: An object that answers -
task.5.summaryItems.3.text: state plus a method that returns a `bool` about that state.
task.5.summaryClose: Next: Control Flow - use these yes/no answers to decide what your program does.

concept.pr-string-concatenation.def: Joining pieces of text (and numbers turned to text) end to end with +.
concept.pr-comparison.def: Asking a yes/no question with == != > < >= <= and getting back a bool.
